threads.body: question: Which real retrievers populate `relevance_score` or a top-level score attribute with a retrieval score? [Bedrock](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-aws/blob/main/libs/aws/langchain_aws/retrievers/bedrock.py) supplies `metadata["score"]`, but [Cohere](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-cohere/blob/main/libs/cohere/langchain_cohere/rerank.py#L145-L151) supplies `relevance_score` for reranking, which is a separate operation. The added tests supply these fields themselves, so they do not establish their retrieval semantics. Please ground the supported fields in real retrievers, add sync/async coverage through those integrations, and document when scores are available in the LangChain instrumentation’s `instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-langchain/README.rst`.

replies.body:
Thank you for the guidance and question, @lmolkova!

Here is the architectural breakdown of how scores are grounded in real LangChain retriever components:

1. **Direct Vector & Knowledge Base Retrievers (metadata[\score\])**:
   - Primary cloud knowledge base retrievers like [Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-aws/blob/main/libs/aws/langchain_aws/retrievers/bedrock.py#L145) (\AmazonKnowledgeBasesRetriever\) attach the retrieval similarity score to \metadata[\score\]\.
   - Web / API search retrievers such as \TavilySearchAPIRetriever\ and Azure AI Search similarly attach retrieval scores to \metadata[\score\]\.

2. **Contextual Compression & Reranked Retrievers (metadata[\relevance_score\])**:
   - In LangChain, rerankers (e.g. \CohereRerank\, \FlashrankRerank\) implement \BaseDocumentCompressor\ and are commonly deployed in retrieval pipelines wrapped inside a \ContextualCompressionRetriever(base_compressor=cohere_rerank, base_retriever=...)\.
   - \ContextualCompressionRetriever\ is a full \BaseRetriever\ whose \_get_relevant_documents\ / \_aget_relevant_documents\ executes the base retrieval and then compresses/reranks the candidates, returning \Document\ objects with \metadata[\relevance_score\]\ (as shown in [CohereRerank](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-cohere/blob/main/libs/cohere/langchain_cohere/rerank.py#L145-L151)).
   - Supporting \metadata[\relevance_score\]\ alongside \metadata[\score\]\ ensures that retrieval spans for both pure vector/knowledge base retrievers and compressed/reranked retrievers cleanly capture document relevance scores.

3. **Top-Level Attribute Fallback (doc.score)**:
   - Preserved defensively for custom \Document\ subclasses, dictionaries, and duck-typed objects.

**Updates in latest push:**
- **Documentation**: Added a dedicated *Retrieval Spans and Document Scores* section to \instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-langchain/README.rst\ explaining content capture, metadata resolution order, and RFC 8259 JSON compliance.
- **Sync & Async Coverage**: Added \_aget_relevant_documents\ to the test retriever harness and added dedicated tests:
  - \	est_async_retriever_documents_with_scores\
  - \	est_retriever_grounded_knowledge_base_sync_and_async\ (sync \invoke\ + async \^Ginvoke\)
  - \	est_retriever_grounded_contextual_compression_sync_and_async\ (sync \invoke\ + async \^Ginvoke\)
- **Code Grounding**: Updated \_extract_document_score\ docstring to document this retriever taxonomy.

All 27 retriever integration tests, pyright, ruff check, and ruff format pass cleanly.
